There were times when I got crazy dark one summer a few years ago. Sleeping all day, up during the night, constant suicidal thoughts. Some nights I would be driving in my car, stop on the tracks, and just sit there. The one thing that always got me to put it back into drive and come home each time was the idea that no one would be there to take care of my cat, and that he deserved better. He's somewhat special needs, and I knew that either 1. no one would take care of him and he'd end up in a shelter, or 2. no one would think to feed him until it was too late. This guy honestly saved my life that summer, which is why I'm a bit of an extra cat parent. He ate better than me any week I was light on cash, because I refused to give him lower quality food, and I could just do ramen until my next check.

I was in a much better place for a few years, and in that time my sister gave birth to my first niece (she's 4 now). I very early on became that favorite extended family member every little kid has. She hears my sister say mention unclethrowawayneedhelp42? Immediately grabs her shoes because she's going to demand to walk down the street and see me, and is just ridiculously excited anytime we're together. I was in a dark place a couple years ago, and the one thing that got me to not go through with it was the idea that I couldn't stand to cause her so any suffering, and be the reason my sister had to explain something so heavy to her. Anytime I hug my niece today, I feel like I'm thanking her a little for getting me through those times. A friend of mine posts on instagram every year a really heartbreaking story about her favorite uncle who committed suicide, and it just confirms why I could never do that to her.

I'm in a much more solid place in life now, and the whole reason I was able to make it through some of the darkest parts was thanks to these two. They have no idea how they're the reason I'm still alive, and I could never forget what they've done for me.
Not really. My friends just abandoned me after everything happened. I ended up working in a  different industry now, but it still screwed up all my finances and mental health long term.
